r7-cap-renamed.title: Hunted class 1: cap renamed rather than removed
r7-cap-renamed.imperative: Establish the SUFFICIENT condition, not the gate's necessary grep: drive the real writer far past 20 active entries from a fresh file, from a legacy cap=20 file, and in one bulk delta; assert every add landed and no int field on the parsed Playbook carries a cap-shaped value.
r7-cap-renamed.finding: HUNTED CLASS 1 -- NOT FOUND. I did not rely on the gate's own grep, which is only necessary: I confirmed all three of my renamed-cap mutants (_BANK_BUDGET refusal, cap= round-trip, silent truncate) pass 'grep -nE DEFAULT_CAP|active cap' cleanly, so that grep cannot carry the verdict. The sufficient condition is behavioural and unbounded, and I established it with probe_unbounded.py driving the REAL writer in-process: (A) fresh file, 300 sequential single-add deltas -> active=300, 0 refusals; (B) the real legacy fixture at 20/20 whose header carries cap=20, +200 adds -> active=220, 0 refusals, and the rendered header comes back 'run-tick=40 dormancy-runs=10 apply-recurrences=1 apply-confirmed=3 ticked-work-ids=...' with cap= dropped; (C) ONE delta carrying 500 adds -> rc=0, active=500. Every case asserts count == adds issued, so a cap implemented as silent truncation rather than refusal would also have shown up. (D) The parsed Playbook's complete int field set is {run_tick, dormancy_runs=10, apply_recurrences=1, apply_confirmed=3} -- no cap-shaped value under any name; the three surviving thresholds are pre-existing per-lesson maturity clocks, none keyed to active-entry count. Static sweep agrees: no comparison against len(book.active) survives anywhere in the writer.

r8-test-can-fail.title: Hunted class 2: replacement test vacuous
r8-test-can-fail.imperative: Determine BY CONSTRUCTION whether tests/test_apply_lessons_delta.py's replacement test can fail. Mutate a COPY of the writer to reintroduce a cap under a different name (one the gate's own grep does not catch), assert the mutation applied, and confirm the test goes red.
r8-test-can-fail.finding: HUNTED CLASS 2 -- NOT FOUND. Determined by construction, not by observing a pass. I built three mutant COPIES of the writer (never touching the file under review), each with the mutation asserted present before the run and each verified to still pass the gate's own grep, then ran the HEAD test module against them: (1) 'refusal' -- a hard cap reintroduced as _BANK_BUDGET=20 raising 'bank budget exhausted' (a cap RENAMED, the exact hunted shape) -> 1 failed, 69 passed; the failure is test_add_past_twenty_succeeds_and_retire_still_deletes. (2) 'render' -- cap=20 round-tripped back into the rendered header -> 2 failed, 68 passed; BOTH new tests fail, including test_legacy_cap_header_parses_and_is_dropped_on_render. (3) 'truncate' -- adds past 20 silently dropped with rc still 0 (a cap that never refuses) -> 1 failed, 69 passed. So the replacement test detects a renamed cap, a grammar-level cap, and a non-refusing cap. It is not vacuous. Baseline for comparison: the same module is 70 passed at HEAD.

r9-grammar.title: playbook-state grammar: legacy tolerance + group renumbering
r9-grammar.imperative: By running code, not reading it: confirm a header carrying cap=N parses and is dropped on render, and that run-tick/dormancy-runs/apply-recurrences/apply-confirmed/ticked-work-ids bind to the right values across EVERY presence combination of the optional groups. Assert the combination count.
r9-grammar.finding: Both halves confirmed BY RUNNING CODE (probe_grammar.py), not by reading the regex. LEGACY TOLERANCE IS REAL: a header carrying cap=N parses without raising, no cap-named attribute survives on the parsed object, and render_playbook drops the field -- re-parsing the rewritten text yields the same values. Confirmed on the real corpus shape too: the actual .agent-work/LESSONS.md header (run-tick=40 cap=20 ... ticked-work-ids=20 ids) round-tripped through +200 adds and came back cap-free. RENUMBERING IS CORRECT: I enumerated ALL 2**4 = 16 presence combinations of the four optional fields (cap / apply-recurrences / apply-confirmed / ticked-work-ids), asserting each of run_tick / dormancy_runs / apply_recurrences / apply_confirmed / ticked_work_ids against DISTINCT sentinels (11 / 22 / 33 / 44 / w-alpha,w-beta) so any swap or off-by-one is detectable, and re-asserting after a render round-trip. Output: 'combinations exercised: 16 (expected 16)', 'failures: 0'. The probe carries a live negative control -- a header with dormancy-runs=77 reads back as 77, not 22, proving the comparison is not vacuously true. Absent-optional-group cases are included (the has_recur=0 / has_conf=0 / has_ticked=0 rows), which is where an off-by-one would hide.
